blockMcqs.question: What does Big-O actually measure?
options: How the work grows as input grows
Wall-clock seconds on a given machine
The memory a program allocates
The number of bugs per line
blockMcqs.explanation: It counts step-growth, which is machine-independent unlike timings.

blockMcqs.question: An input limit of n ≤ 20 most likely hints at:
options: An O(n) single-pass solution
An O(n log n) sorting solution
An O(2ⁿ) bitmask or backtracking solution
An O(1) closed-form formula
blockMcqs.explanation: Tiny n tolerates exponential work, signalling subset or backtracking.

blockMcqs.question: How do O/Ω/Θ relate to worst/average/best case?
options: They are the same thing
Big-O always means worst case
They are independent axes
Θ only describes the best case
blockMcqs.explanation: One picks which input; the other describes the growth shape.

blockMcqs.question: What is the complexity of `for (i = 1; i < n; i *= 2)`?
options: O(n)
O(n²)
O(log n)
blockMcqs.explanation: Doubling the index reaches n in about log₂n iterations.

blockMcqs.question: Solve T(n) = 2·T(n/2) + n with the Master Theorem.
options: Θ(n)
Θ(n²)
Θ(log n)
Θ(n log n)
blockMcqs.explanation: Leaf cost equals f(n), so it lands in case 2 with a log factor.

blockMcqs.question: Why is appending to a doubling dynamic array O(1) amortized?
options: Resizes never copy any elements
Each append is individually constant time
The array preallocates infinite capacity
Rare O(n) resizes get exponentially further apart
blockMcqs.explanation: Total copy work stays under 2n, so the average per push is constant.

blockMcqs.question: Why do sort libraries use insertion sort for tiny subarrays?
options: Insertion sort has a better Big-O class
Its low constants win on small inputs
Quicksort cannot sort fewer than ten items
It guarantees O(log n) on any input
blockMcqs.explanation: Asymptotics ignore constants, which dominate when n is small.

blockMcqs.question: Why did Java's HashMap start treeifying long buckets?
options: To preserve insertion order of keys
To shrink memory used per entry
To bound worst-case lookup at O(log n)
To make every lookup exactly O(1)
blockMcqs.explanation: A tree caps a degenerate collision chain that would otherwise be O(n).
